The pointer only moves while a finger is on the touch area, so it stays put when you put the pen down or gesture with it.
The pointer follows every movement of the pen, like a laser pointer. Handy for presenting, but it also moves while you hold the pen otherwise.

How the app tells your touches on the touch area apart:

1. You touch the area and let go. If your finger was there for less than the longest tap, it's a tap. Otherwise you were holding it to move the pointer, and nothing else happens.
2. After a tap, the app waits briefly to see whether you tap again.
3. If a second tap comes in that time, the two taps are a double tap. If not, it was a single tap.

Touch the area below to try it: the card shows how long your last touch was.

Touches up to %1$s count as a tap (single tap: %2$s). Keep your finger on the area longer than that to move the pointer instead. If your taps sometimes don\'t register, move this to the right. If holding sometimes counts as a tap, move it to the left.

After a tap the app waits %1$s for a second one. Single tap: %2$s, about %1$s after you let go. Two taps within that time are a double tap: %3$s, and the single-tap action doesn\'t run. Shorter makes single taps faster, but you\'ll need to double tap faster too.

Instant: a single tap (%1$s) runs the moment you let go, with no delay. The catch: a double tap is two taps, so its first touch runs the single-tap action too, then the double tap (%2$s) follows. Works best if one of the two actions is harmless, e.g. Nothing.

Choose the texture and strength for each tool

Saber itself is not modified. This app uses an accessibility service to detect when Saber\'s window is focused. With root, it reads Saber\'s settings file to see the active tool, and adds a virtual stylus button that Android merges with the pen\'s input. Saber\'s developers aren\'t involved and aren\'t responsible for this, so please don\'t report problems with it to Saber.
